etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English silver, selver, sulver, from Old English seolfor, from Proto-West Germanic *silubr, from Proto-Germanic *silubrą (“silver”), of uncertain origin.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) A lustrous, white, metallic element, atomic number 47, atomic weight 107.87, symbol Ag.
(collectively) Coins made from silver or any similar white metal.

quote.citation: 1990, David F. Friedman, Don DeNevi, A Youth in Babylon: Confessions of a Trash-film King, page 136:
quote.text: […]  maybe two or three twenties, a dozen tens, and twenty or thirty fins. The rest is all aces and silver.

definitions.definition: (collectively) Cutlery and other eating utensils, whether silver or made from some other white metal.
(collectively) Any items made from silver or any other white metal.

quote.citation: 2017, Sam Shepard, chapter 27, in Spy of the First Person, →ISBN, page 62:
quote.text: I'll need some mayonnaise and a silver tin of sardines, a banana.

definitions.definition: Anything resembling silver; something shiny and white.

quote.citation: 1909 April 10, H[erbert] G[eorge] Wells, “[The Time Machine and Other Stories]. The Beautiful Suit.”, in The Short Stories of H. G. Wells, London: Ernest Benn Limited […], published September 1927, →OCLC, pages 162–163:
quote.text: And next morning they found him dead, with his neck broken, in the bottom of the stone pit, with his beautiful clothes a little bloody, and foul and stained with the duckweed from the pond. But his face was a face of such happiness that, had you seen it, you would have understood indeed how that he had died happy, never knowing that cool and streaming silver for the duckweed in the pond.

quote.citation: 1918, W[illiam] B[abington] Maxwell, chapter X, in The Mirror and the Lamp, Indianapolis, Ind.: The Bobbs-Merrill Company, →OCLC:
quote.text: He looked round the poor room, at the distempered walls, and the bad engravings in meretricious frames, the crinkly paper and wax flowers on the chiffonier; and he thought of a room like Father Bryan's, with panelling, with cut glass, with tulips in silver pots, such a room as he had hoped to have for his own.

quote.citation: 1959, Georgette Heyer, chapter 1, in The Unknown Ajax:
quote.text: But Richmond […] appeared to lose himself in his own reflections. Some pickled crab, which he had not touched, had been removed with a damson pie; and his sister saw, peeping around the massive silver epergne that almost obscured him from her view, that he had eaten no more than a spoonful of that either.

definitions.definition: Having a color like silver: a shiny gray.
Denoting the twenty-fifth anniversary, especially of a wedding.

quote.citation: 1994, “Mate matching” in Accent on Living, v 38, n 4 (Spring), p 52:
quote.text: Mostly, these have been relationships of 10 or less years. However, one respondent has celebrated her silver wedding anniversary.

definitions.definition: (of commercial services) Premium, but inferior to gold.
Having the clear, musical tone of silver; soft and clear in sound.

quote.citation: 1880 November 12, Lew[is] Wallace, chapter IV, in Ben-Hur: A Tale of the Christ, New York, N.Y.: Harper & Brothers, […], →OCLC, book sixth, page 416:
quote.text: Presently all the eastern sky began to silver and shine, and objects before invisible in the west—chiefly the tall towers on Mount Zion—emerged as from a shadowy depth, [...]

quote.citation: 1907 August, Robert W[illiam] Chambers, “Silverside”, in The Younger Set, New York, N.Y.: D. Appleton & Company, →OCLC, page 281:
quote.text: But when the moon rose and the breeze awakened, and the sedges stirred, and the cat's-paws raced across the moonlit ponds, and the far surf off Wonder Head intoned the hymn of the four winds, the trinity, earth and sky and water, became one thunderous symphony—a harmony of sound and colour silvered to a monochrome by the moon.

definitions.definition: To cover with silver, or with a silvery metal.
To polish like silver; to impart a brightness to, like that of silver.

quote.citation: 1725, Homer, “Book X”, in [Alexander Pope], transl., The Odyssey of Homer. […], volume III, London:  […]  Bernard Lintot, →OCLC, page 17, lines 107–108:
quote.text: For here retir'd the ſinking billows ſleep, / And ſmiling calmneſs ſilver'd o'er the deep.

definitions.definition: To make hoary, or white, like silver.

quote.citation: 1727, [John] Gay, “Introduction to the Fables. The Shepherd and the Philosopher.”, in Fables, 2nd edition, volume I, London:  […] J[acob] Tonson and J. Watts, published 1728, →OCLC:
quote.text: Remote from cities liv'd a Swain, / Unvex'd with all the cares of gain, / His head was ſilver'd o'er with age, / And long experience made him ſage; [...]
